# US-007 — Board, List, and Search

**Story ID:** US-007  
**Priority:** P1  
**Tasks:** T-010 (UI), T-011 (data logic)  
**Status:** Shipped (QA PASS)

## Who uses this and why

A planr user who wants to see all work organised in the familiar Kanban column
format (Board), browse and filter all artifacts in a dense table (List), or jump
to any artifact instantly by typing a few characters without navigating through
menus (Search/⌘K). These three views complement the hierarchical Graph view with
flat, work-centric perspectives on the same artifact set.

## What it does

### Board view (`lib/dashboard/app/views/board.js`)

The Board renders four status columns: Outstanding · In Progress · Blocked · Done.
Each column has a count badge. Artifacts appear as `ds-cardlet` components showing
a type-accent strip, the artifact id, title, and a footer with the status label.

A "Group by" toolbar lets the user regroup the board by status (default), sprint,
or feature. `groupBy(nodes, key)` is exported from `board.js`; it returns an
ordered `Map`:

- Status grouping: Outstanding → In Progress → Blocked → Done order.
- Sprint grouping: keyed by the `sprintId` frontmatter field.
- Feature grouping: keyed by the `featureId` frontmatter field.

The Board re-renders when a `planr:filter-change` event fires on `document`
(Status or Type filter changed in the rail). No drag-to-move interactions exist —
zero `dragstart`, `dragover`, `drop`, or `contenteditable` references in the file.

### List view (`lib/dashboard/app/views/list.js`)

The List renders a dense sortable table with a type-chip filter toolbar. The
toolbar offers type chips: Epic / Feature / Story / Task / Spec. Columns are: id,
title, type, status, updated — all are sortable (click the column header). The
header row is sticky.

`filterNodes(nodes, filterState)` and `sortNodes(nodes, sortKey, direction)` are
both pure functions (no DOM side-effects) exported from `list.js`. Filtering is
client-side — no server round-trip on chip click. The view re-renders on both
`planr:filter-change` and `planr:sort-change` events.

On mobile, the table scrolls horizontally inside its card container rather than
squishing the columns (per design-spec §3 reflow notes).

### Search view / ⌘K overlay (`lib/dashboard/app/views/search.js`)

The Search overlay is a command palette that sits above all other content. It is
activated by ⌘K / Ctrl+K from anywhere in the app (via `cmdkDispatcher` in
`main.js`) or by clicking the ⌘K field in the top bar.

The overlay renders: a scrim (click to close), a focused input, a result list
showing artifact id + title + type chip, and keyboard navigation hints.

`buildIndex(nodes)` constructs a character-trigram index over `node.id` and
`node.title`. `query(index, term)` computes trigram intersection scores and
returns the top 20 results ranked by score. `KeyNavState(items)` manages keyboard
cursor state: `moveDown()`, `moveUp()` (both clamp), `getActive()` returns null at
index -1, and `reset(newItems)` resets the cursor when the result list changes.

Keyboard behaviour: ↑/↓ moves the cursor, Enter navigates to `#detail/<id>`,
Escape closes the overlay. `open()` and `close()` are exported for external callers
(`cmdkDispatcher` and the top-bar field).

## Acceptance criteria (all passing)

- Board: four status columns with count badges; `ds-cardlet` cards with type accent, id, title, status footer; Group-by toolbar for status/sprint/feature; read-only (no drag events).
- List: type-chip filter toolbar; sortable columns (id, title, type, status, updated); sticky header; client-side filter with no server round-trip.
- Search: scrim overlay with auto-focused input; result list; fuzzy match updating as user types (max 20 results); keyboard navigation ↑/↓/Enter/Escape.
- ⌘K / Ctrl+K activates the overlay from anywhere; top-bar field click also activates.
- Zero off-palette hex values in board.js, list.js, search.js (Python-verified by QA).
- `groupBy` produces correct column order (Outstanding → In Progress → Blocked → Done).
- `filterNodes` and `sortNodes` are pure functions.
- No npm package imports in any modified file (stdlib JS only).
